synthesis.crowd_consensus: Failure of the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI), the private telecom backbone operated by L3Harris that carries controller-pilot radio between Air Route Traffic Control Centers and remote transmitters. CBS (multiple sources): an update to the L3Harris-operated private communications network caused it to reboot, leading to a crash and comms outage. WSJ (people briefed): outage in the L3Harris-overseen network handling crucial ATC radio frequencies. Official line (Sec. Mullin, White House briefing; Sec. Duffy; AP): "introduction of some new technology into an old air traffic control system overwhelmed it" — new routers/equipment/patches overloaded the legacy system; press-conference wording "routers overloaded with data", with cyber/rogue-AI not fully ruled out.
synthesis.best_technical_mechanism: tjohns maps the comms stack (Collins/ARINC = oceanic HF, FAA TechOps = VHF, L3Harris = inter-facility backhaul), matching the official "communications issue impacting all ARTCCs" framing (50492033). Null-Set hypothesizes IP-over-legacy bridging where TCP retransmit storms drowned legacy TDM components, consistent with officials noting the new IP routers showed no inconsistency (50493513). Animats counters that a TDM multiplexer cannot be "overloaded", pointing to the link-assignment/switch layer or a fiber cut, and discounts political-appointee explanations (50493802).
synthesis.precedent_context: Alexsky2 links the 2009 DOT OIG report on the FTI (Harris) outage — same TDM-era architecture, analogous failure mode, 20,982 services on FTI (50493456). mzs cites the September 2026 Washington-region comms failure: circuit failed and contractors had ripped through the backup fiber (50491302). jiggawatts: FTI was built 2002-2007, well inside the IP era (50492721).
